events.name: FIFA World Cup 2026: Argentina v Switzerland
events.description: Argentina v Switzerland (Kick-off 2.00am). Coverage of the fourth quarter-final, which takes place at Kansas City Stadium in the USA. Current World Cup holders Argentina survived an almighty scare in the last round as they came from 2-0 down to win 3-2 against Egypt. The African side had gone two goals ahead with 23 minutes remaining but three goals inside 13 minutes from Cristian Romero, Lionel Messi and Enzo Fernandez saw Argentina progress to their second successive quarter-final in this competition. Switzerland reached their first quarter-final since 1954 after they beat Colombia 4-3 on penalties after the game finished 0-0 in Vancouver. Before Tuesday's victory the European side had reached the round-of-16 at the last three World Cups, but heroics from goalkeeper Gregor Kobel ended that run and helped them reach this stage for the first time in 72 years

Some of the greatest matches in World Cup history have taken place at this stage of the tournament, including a 1958 encounter between Brazil and France, when a 17-year-old Pele scored a 23-minute hat-trick in a 5-2 victory, while 1970 saw Italy triumph 4-3 over West Germany in Mexico, with five of the seven goals scored in extra time in a game many will remember for Franz Beckenbauer playing with his arm in a makeshift sling after dislocating his shoulder. The West Germans avenged that loss 12 years later with a penalty shootout victory in Spain in one of the most controversial matches in history, which saw West German goalkeeper Harald Schumacher deliberately collide with French player Patrick Battiston, knocking him unconscious and forcing him from the game with two missing teeth and three cracked ribs. Schumacher didn't even receive a yellow card and kept goal for the remainder of the match, which his side won on penalties after a thrilling 3-3 draw, in what was the first-ever World Cup finals match to be decided by spot kicks

event.description: Argentina v Switzerland (Kick-off 2.00am). Coverage of the fourth quarter-final, which takes place at Kansas City Stadium in the USA. Current World Cup holders Argentina survived an almighty scare in the last round as they came from 2-0 down to win 3-2 against Egypt. The African side had gone two goals ahead with 23 minutes remaining but three goals inside 13 minutes from Cristian Romero, Lionel Messi and Enzo Fernandez saw Argentina progress to their second successive quarter-final in this competition. Switzerland reached their first quarter-final since 1954 after they beat Colombia 4-3 on penalties after the game finished 0-0 in Vancouver. Before Tuesday's victory the European side had reached the round-of-16 at the last three World Cups, but heroics from goalkeeper Gregor Kobel ended that run and helped them reach this stage for the first time in 72 years

The West Germans avenged that loss 12 years later with a penalty shootout victory in Spain in one of the most controversial matches in history, which saw West German goalkeeper Harald Schumacher deliberately collide with French player Patrick Battiston, knocking him unconscious and forcing him from the game with two missing teeth and three cracked ribs. Schumacher didn't even receive a yellow card and kept goal for the remainder of the match, which his side won on penalties after a thrilling 3-3 draw, in what was the first-ever World Cup finals match to be decided by spot kicks
